bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Data security and patient-data privacy — Identified as a BRSR material issue (risk and opportunity). Data security threats can compromise the security and integrity of the Company's IT systems; a breach of patient or stakeholder data may expose HCG to litigation, fines and penalties and the loss of valuable data. Mitigation rests on regular vulnerability and breach-threat assessments, employee cybersecurity training and periodic awareness mailers. The risk grows as HCG digitises the patient journey and centralises EMR, HIS and ERP data.
- Business ethics, corporate governance and regulatory compliance — BRSR material issue. Failure to comply with the highest standards of corporate governance and business ethics can lead to regulatory consequences and financial or reputational damage, affecting business continuity. Managed through proactive engagement with regulators across facilities and mandatory training on business ethics and the code of conduct. Relevant given the volume of related-party dealings disclosed (promoter-family professional and consultancy fees, transactions with promoter-linked trusts and academies).
- Occupational health and safety across the hospital network — BRSR material issue rated a pure risk. Ineffective health and safety management programmes could cause a significant increase in incidents, which would hurt employee well-being, brand image and reputation and thereby the ability to attract and retain talent - a direct threat for a business whose output depends on scarce specialist clinicians. Mitigated by an Employee Health and Safety Policy, targeted training, Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) applied to all services, and rigorous Quality Audits.
- Waste management and disposal (including biomedical waste) — BRSR material issue. Poor management and disposal of waste can harm human health and the environment, cause financial losses and legal repercussions for non-compliance with laws and regulations, and significantly compromise the Company's brand value. Mitigation is proper-disposal arrangements plus continuous efforts to enhance waste recycling.
- Water dependence and water-efficiency exposure — BRSR material issue rated a pure risk. Water usage is extensive across HCG's hospitals given the nature of operations, so poor water management can create scarcity that materially affects business continuity and growth and erodes brand value. Managed through regular monitoring of water usage at all locations, water meters installed at all discharge sites, and recycling and reuse technologies.
- Underperformance and impairment of acquired or newer centres — The Board's Report records exceptional items for FY 2025-26 comprising an additional impairment provision against the investment in HCG Kolkata Cancer Care LLP and an impairment loss on remeasurement of the investment in BACC Health Care classified as held for sale, partly offset by an impairment reversal on HCG Manavata Oncology LLP. Since growth depends on commissioning greenfield centres and integrating acquisitions, individual units failing to ramp is a recurring, structural drag rather than a one-off.
- Dependence on inorganic growth amid consolidation of the Indian healthcare sector — Management states that increasing consolidation in the Indian healthcare sector presents both challenges and opportunities and makes it imperative to actively pursue organic and inorganic growth avenues. That raises competition for assets, execution and integration risk, and the risk of overpaying, while remaining minority interests - such as the balance 15% of Vizag Hospital still to be acquired under the Shareholders' Agreement - leave future purchase obligations open.
- Partially owned subsidiaries, step-down structures and international exposure — A large part of the network runs through LLPs and companies held at less than 100% (for example 51%, 70.25%, 74%, 78.60% and 84.89% stakes), which constrains control over cash flows and requires partner alignment. The overseas chain runs through Mauritius holding vehicles into Kenya and Uganda, adding jurisdictional and currency exposure; the non-operating Tanzania subsidiary was wound up with effect from March 02, 2026, and the Kenyan associate reports on a different calendar.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Drive sustainable and profitable growth through disciplined, capital-efficient investments that maximize returns while minimizing risk, with a stated vision to be the market leader in every geography HCG operates in
- Expand the reach of the cancer care network in India by establishing new HCG cancer centres and augmenting capacity and service offerings at existing locations, with site selection driven by a competitive market assessment (cancer incidence in the catchment, existing comprehensive centres, patient travel distance, affordability, and available third-party payer options)
- Grow inorganically through strategic acquisitions and stake consolidation - the 51% Vizag Hospital acquisition in October 2024 followed by an additional 34% on April 13, 2026 taking holding to 85%
- Strengthen the HCG brand to reach more cancer patients through technological excellence, high clinical standards, patient support groups involving cancer survivors, and screening-awareness and community-education programmes
- Improve accessibility and reduce patient travel through hub-and-spoke day-care facilities that deepen brand presence in local communities
- Maintain technology leadership in oncology by pioneering next-generation diagnostic and treatment modalities - CyberKnife, Digital PET-CT, TomoTherapy, MR-LINAC - to lift both patient outcomes and operational efficiency
- Invest in a robust private-cloud IT infrastructure integrating centralized EMR, HIS and ERP systems to enable seamless care coordination, protocol refinement, longitudinal studies and biorepository integration, positioning HCG as a partner of choice for academic and clinical research
- Strengthen the patient-engagement technology ecosystem via an advanced CRM platform, a Patient Application, a Doctor's Application and a technology-driven call centre to improve operational efficiency, patient follow-up and sales productivity
- Sharpen focus on the core oncology business by divesting non-core assets - the entire equity shareholding in BACC Health Care (Milann fertility business) was divested on June 29, 2026 to unlock value and redeploy capital
- Retain profits for reinvestment into the business rather than distributing them, in alignment with the organic and inorganic growth strategy
- Build a clinician-talent advantage by offering participation in academics, clinical trials and research with mentorship and research grants through India's largest oncologist community
- Expand the Ahmedabad facility's service depth beyond TomoTherapy, robotic surgical systems and scalp cooling therapy to include genetic counselling, international services, home and palliative care and peer support
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: HCG frames expansion as disciplined, capital-efficient growth across four tracks. (1) Greenfield: it reports a strong pipeline of new centres in high-potential markets and a proven capability to commission and scale new facilities; the flagship recent addition is the new comprehensive cancer hospital at Hebbal, North Bengaluru, launched on May 19, 2026 with up to 132 beds and Karnataka's first Elekta Unity MR-Linac, designed as a full-spectrum oncology centre. (2) Brownfield and core-platform work: focused brownfield expansion across key hospitals to optimise existing infrastructure and capacity, improved capacity utilisation and operating efficiency across centres, and structured turnaround plans to strengthen performance and scale up newer centres. (3) Inorganic: targeted acquisitions to accelerate entry into new geographies, with a demonstrated integration model - having taken 51% of Mahatma Gandhi Cancer Hospital & Research Institute (Vizag Hospital) in October 2024, HCG completed the purchase of a further 34% on April 13, 2026 to reach 85%. (4) Adjacencies: asset-light day-care centres acting as access points and feeders to tertiary hospitals, plus expansion into complementary segments such as diagnostics, clinical trials and pharmacy, and wider access for international patients. Underpinning all four is continued technology investment - maintaining leadership in medical technology and end-to-end digitisation of the patient journey. Management links the expansion to India's demand-supply gap in oncology infrastructure and a structural shift in patient preference towards comprehensive cancer care centres over conventional multi-specialty hospitals. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle.

risks.note: Identified as a BRSR material issue (risk and opportunity). Data security threats can compromise the security and integrity of the Company's IT systems; a breach of patient or stakeholder data may expose HCG to litigation, fines and penalties and the loss of valuable data. Mitigation rests on regular vulnerability and breach-threat assessments, employee cybersecurity training and periodic awareness mailers. The risk grows as HCG digitises the patient journey and centralises EMR, HIS and ERP data.

BRSR material issue. Failure to comply with the highest standards of corporate governance and business ethics can lead to regulatory consequences and financial or reputational damage, affecting business continuity. Managed through proactive engagement with regulators across facilities and mandatory training on business ethics and the code of conduct. Relevant given the volume of related-party dealings disclosed (promoter-family professional and consultancy fees, transactions with promoter-linked trusts and academies).
risks.risk: Business ethics, corporate governance and regulatory compliance

risks.note: BRSR material issue rated a pure risk. Ineffective health and safety management programmes could cause a significant increase in incidents, which would hurt employee well-being, brand image and reputation and thereby the ability to attract and retain talent - a direct threat for a business whose output depends on scarce specialist clinicians. Mitigated by an Employee Health and Safety Policy, targeted training, Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) applied to all services, and rigorous Quality Audits.
risks.risk: Occupational health and safety across the hospital network

risks.note: BRSR material issue. Poor management and disposal of waste can harm human health and the environment, cause financial losses and legal repercussions for non-compliance with laws and regulations, and significantly compromise the Company's brand value. Mitigation is proper-disposal arrangements plus continuous efforts to enhance waste recycling.
risks.risk: Waste management and disposal (including biomedical waste)

risks.note: BRSR material issue rated a pure risk. Water usage is extensive across HCG's hospitals given the nature of operations, so poor water management can create scarcity that materially affects business continuity and growth and erodes brand value. Managed through regular monitoring of water usage at all locations, water meters installed at all discharge sites, and recycling and reuse technologies.

The Board's Report records exceptional items for FY 2025-26 comprising an additional impairment provision against the investment in HCG Kolkata Cancer Care LLP and an impairment loss on remeasurement of the investment in BACC Health Care classified as held for sale, partly offset by an impairment reversal on HCG Manavata Oncology LLP. Since growth depends on commissioning greenfield centres and integrating acquisitions, individual units failing to ramp is a recurring, structural drag rather than a one-off.
risks.risk: Underperformance and impairment of acquired or newer centres

Mitigated by an Employee Health and Safety Policy, targeted training, Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) applied to all services, and rigorous Quality Audits.

risks.risk: Waste management and disposal (including biomedical waste)
risks.note: BRSR material issue. Poor management and disposal of waste can harm human health and the environment, cause financial losses and legal repercussions for non-compliance with laws and regulations, and significantly compromise the Company's brand value. Mitigation is proper-disposal arrangements plus continuous efforts to enhance waste recycling.

BRSR material issue rated a pure risk. Water usage is extensive across HCG's hospitals given the nature of operations, so poor water management can create scarcity that materially affects business continuity and growth and erodes brand value. Managed through regular monitoring of water usage at all locations, water meters installed at all discharge sites, and recycling and reuse technologies.

risks.risk: Underperformance and impairment of acquired or newer centres
risks.note: The Board's Report records exceptional items for FY 2025-26 comprising an additional impairment provision against the investment in HCG Kolkata Cancer Care LLP and an impairment loss on remeasurement of the investment in BACC Health Care classified as held for sale, partly offset by an impairment reversal on HCG Manavata Oncology LLP. Since growth depends on commissioning greenfield centres and integrating acquisitions, individual units failing to ramp is a recurring, structural drag rather than a one-off.

risks.risk: Dependence on inorganic growth amid consolidation of the Indian healthcare sector
risks.note: Management states that increasing consolidation in the Indian healthcare sector presents both challenges and opportunities and makes it imperative to actively pursue organic and inorganic growth avenues. That raises competition for assets, execution and integration risk, and the risk of overpaying, while remaining minority interests - such as the balance 15% of Vizag Hospital still to be acquired under the Shareholders' Agreement - leave future purchase obligations open.

risks.note: A large part of the network runs through LLPs and companies held at less than 100% (for example 51%, 70.25%, 74%, 78.60% and 84.89% stakes), which constrains control over cash flows and requires partner alignment. one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: HealthCare Global Enterprises is India's cancer care specialist, operating the country's largest private cancer care network in terms of the number of comprehensive cancer centres, complemented by an oncology diagnostics arm and multispecialty hospitals.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: HCG is a super-specialty healthcare provider with a strategic focus on oncology, running comprehensive cancer centres under the HCG brand that bring diagnosis, molecular pathology and imaging, radiation therapy, nuclear medicine and surgical oncology together under one roof. It complements this with Triesta Sciences, an integrated oncology diagnostics platform spanning laboratory services, R&D and clinical research, and with multispecialty hospitals delivering tertiary and quaternary care across cardiac sciences, orthopedics, neurosciences, nephrology and gastroenterology. It served insured, self-paying and government-scheme patients across India and, until the June 2026 divestment of BACC Health Care, also ran the Milann fertility business.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: HCG frames expansion as disciplined, capital-efficient growth across four tracks. (1) Greenfield: it reports a strong pipeline of new centres in high-potential markets and a proven capability to commission and scale new facilities; the flagship recent addition is the new comprehensive cancer hospital at Hebbal, North Bengaluru, launched on May 19, 2026 with up to 132 beds and Karnataka's first Elekta Unity MR-Linac, designed as a full-spectrum oncology centre. (2) Brownfield and core-platform work: focused brownfield expansion across key hospitals to optimise existing infrastructure and capacity, improved capacity utilisation and operating efficiency across centres, and structured turnaround plans to strengthen performance and scale up newer centres. (3) Inorganic: targeted acquisitions to accelerate entry into new geographies, with a demonstrated integration model - having taken 51% of Mahatma Gandhi Cancer Hospital & Research Institute (Vizag Hospital) in October 2024, HCG completed the purchase of a further 34% on April 13, 2026 to reach 85%. (4) Adjacencies: asset-light day-care centres acting as access points and feeders to tertiary hospitals, plus expansion into complementary segments such as diagnostics, clinical trials and pharmacy, and wider access for international patients. Underpinning all four is continued technology investment - maintaining leadership in medical technology and end-to-end digitisation of the patient journey. Management links the expansion to India's demand-supply gap in oncology infrastructure and a structural shift in patient preference towards comprehensive cancer care centres over conventional multi-specialty hospitals. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle.

management_tone.body: Confident, disciplined, and strategically focused; Emphasis on 'profitable growth' over pure topline chasing; Transparent on intentional revenue trade-offs for margin quality; Bullish on clinical differentiation as a moat.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Network scale and brand: operates India's largest private cancer care network in terms of the number of comprehensive cancer centres, with the HCG brand described as a powerful differentiator in the Indian oncology landscape
- Operating leverage from case volume: high volume of patient cases enables economies of scale through optimal utilization of equipment, technologies and specialist expertise, supporting a competitive cost structure
- Technology leadership demonstrated by a record of Indian firsts - first private cancer centre in India to introduce Cyclotron and PET-CT, one of the first with CyberKnife, first Radixact system, first Varian Ethos, first Digital PET-CT, and Karnataka's first Elekta Unity MR-Linac at the new North Bengaluru facility
- Standardised, multi-disciplinary clinical protocols deployed uniformly across the network, delivering consistent quality of care across geographies
- Vertically integrated oncology diagnostics through Triesta Sciences, described as one of the country's largest networks of CAP- and NABL-accredited oncology diagnostic laboratories
- Clinician-talent flywheel: access to India's largest oncologist community with mentorship and research grants, where higher patient inflow translates into professional growth and makes HCG a destination of choice for top oncology talent
- Broad payer access from empanelment under CGHS, ECHS and other central and state government health programmes alongside private insurance and self-pay
- Institutional backing with KKR as co-promoter and a strengthened leadership structure under Dr. Manish Mattoo as CEO
- Emerging research ecosystem in Bengaluru spanning Genomics, Proteomics, Molecular Oncology, CAR-T therapies and Organoid-based research platforms

- Expand the reach of the cancer care network in India by establishing new HCG cancer centres and augmenting capacity and service offerings at existing locations, with site selection driven by a competitive market assessment (cancer incidence in the catchment, existing comprehensive centres, patient travel distance, affordability, and available third-party payer options)

themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.
